text:
Alex K: Quick sync — I'm prototyping a tiny 'client-policy-shim' for SDKs so older clients can run with new routing/quota headers without server-side rollouts. Wanted to float tradeoffs.

Maya R: curious, what's the exact problem this fixes?

Alex K: When control plane flips to 'route-by-policy' some requests need header X-Route-Policy or we misattribute quotas to default pools. New servers assume header present. Older SDKs don't send it until upgraded -> spikes and wrong billing.

Ryan C: so shim adds a client-side header generator? that sounds like it could leak decisions to clients.

Alex K: Not generator. It maps legacy route tags to the new header using a tiny compatibility table derived from config. Only runs when negotiation fails (server returns 428 or a specific telemetry tag). Opt-in via env var for now.

Lina S: What about telemetry? We already sample metrics based on header presence. If we synthesize headers at client, console dashboards will look like traffic changed.

Alex K: Good point. Plan is to set an internal opentelemetry attribute: sdk.policy_shim = "synthesized" so console can filter/shade those in dashboards and cost rollups.

Sam T: I'm worried about it being a breaking contract for enterprises — some customers rely on explicit routing. If SDK silently adds header, we could violate isolation.

Alex K: Won't be silent by default. Default: shim disabled. Rollout path: enable on clients in small percentage for internal infra, collect signal, then allow customers to opt-in. For private deployments we won't ship the table unless admin enables.

Maya R: Can we make the shim a CLI/SDK flag that returns a non-zero code if it detects misconfiguration? e.g., `REDWOOD_CLIENT_POLICY_SHIM=warn` vs `=enforce`

Alex K: Yeah — propose values: off|warn|enforce. warn logs a telemetry event and sets attribute, enforce adds header and retries.

Ryan C: How about the server side? We'll need a graceful indicator so SDKs can detect 'need header' without guessing. Maybe return 409 + header "X-Need-Policy:1".

Lina S: 409 used a lot. prefer 428 or 412? we already have a little dance for handshake in the routing layer.

Alex K: Implementation idea: 428 (precondition required) + body {"need_policy":true, "policy_hint":"<name>"} so SDKs can map. That body should be small.

Sam T: For telemetry sampling, add a metric `sdk.policy_shim.invocations` and tag with client_version, mode (warn|enforce). We can surface in console as a tile.

Maya R: UX request: console should show "shim coverage" by app key and allow filtering cost graphs to exclude shim-attributed tokens.

Lina S: We'll also need docs for legal/enterprise admins. If they turn on strict isolation, the shim must never auto-enable.

Alex K: Agreed. We'll respect `admin.allow_client_shim=false` in control plane. Default false for enterprise orgs.

Ryan C: One more: GC and memory. The table might be big for old clients. Keep it < 2kb. Prefer server-driven tiny hints not full tables.

Alex K: We'll ship small mapping and rely on server hints when possible. Fallback local table only for first-gen compatibility.

Sam T: Tests? add integration test where server returns 428 and SDK with env=warn logs the event but does not resend with header; with env=enforce it resends and succeeds.

Maya R: Can we add a telemetry flag so customer ops can opt out of collecting shim metrics? compliance demand sometimes.

Alex K: We'll support `telemetry.shim_enabled=false` per org. Telemetry team will expose a compliance toggle.

deploy-bot: staging canary: client-policy-shim v0.1 deployed to internal-canary, traffic=1% :rocket:

Lina S: Ok next steps: Alex to PR SDK shim (py + ts + go) with opt-in env flags, Ryan to spec server 428+hint response, Sam to add metrics, Maya to draft console tile mock, I'll draft enterprise docs. We'll reconvene after canary runs for 48h.

Alex K: I'll open the PRs tonight and add the test harness. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
